title: runtime-side-schema-probe-optin-v3-proxy-shim
author: Priya Verma
description: Motivation: Several customers surfaced intermittent failures when calling tool/function envelopes while we rolled out schema v3. We want a runtime-side, opt-in probe that detects client schema capability at request time, collects telemetry for gradual rollout, and applies a safe shim to preserve streaming and structured output guarantees. This PR adds a lightweight schema probe middleware to the proxy that inspects a single probe token at the start of the request when the client sets X-Redwood-Schema: v3-beta. The middleware implements: 1) a non-blocking probe step that attempts a minimal handshake compatible with v3 tool envelopes; 2) a fast-path toggle so probe cost is removed after capability confirmation for that session ID; 3) a deterministic fallback to v2 envelope semantics on explicit failure or timeout to preserve availability. The approach intentionally keeps changes on the runtime/proxy surface so most models and serving runtime paths remain untouched. Implementation details: Added runtime proxy middleware and header parsing in pkg/openai/compat to surface client-declared capability. Probe uses a single-token interaction and a 150ms timeout by default; failures are logged and increment a new metric openai_compat.schema_probe.failures. We added a short-lived session cache keyed by client-request-id to avoid repeated probes for the same client in quick succession. Telemetry and rollout plan: Emitted metrics include openai_compat.schema_probe.attempts, .successes, .failures, and .slow_path_count. We also emit labelled metrics by org_id and header value to measure adoption. Rollout: feature is gated behind a runtime flag and requires clients to opt in with X-Redwood-Schema: v3-beta to participate. Initial rollout will enable the probe for 5% of eligible traffic (canary) and then scale in 10% increments once failure rate <0.5%. Compatibility guarantees: If probe fails or times out, request is automatically coerced to v2-compatible envelope semantics with preserved streaming; structured output coercion is applied only when safe. Tests and docs: End-to-end tests simulating mixed v2/v3 clients added; a new doc page describes the opt-in header, telemetry, and migration guidance. Security and privacy: probes do not send customer payloads to external services and telemetry is aggregated. Checklist: - [x] add probe middleware and header parsing - [x] metrics and telemetry tagging - [x] unit and e2e tests - [x] docs and migration guidance - [x] runtime toggle and canary config - [x] update changelog and console release notes
commits: feat(proxy): add runtime schema probe middleware and session cache
feat(compat): parse X-Redwood-Schema header and expose capability checks
perf(cache): make probe cache LRU with 1000-key default
test(e2e): add mixed v2/v3 client scenarios for streaming and tool-calls
docs: add openai_compat/schema_v3_migration.md and canary rollout notes
chore: add telemetry metrics and Prometheus labels
fix(proxy): tighten probe timeout handling to avoid blocking streaming threads
review_comments: Luca: This looks good but please add a unit test for header parsing edge cases (missing header, malformed value).
Priya: Added header parsing unit tests and included a small fuzz harness to catch malformed values. See commit feat(compat): parse X-Redwood-Schema header and expose capability checks.
Anya: Can we ensure the probe cache respects multi-tenant isolation? I don't want a session id collision to leak capability state across orgs.
Priya: Cache is keyed by org_id + client-request-id now. Updated session_cache.go and added tests to assert isolation.
Ben: The 150ms timeout seems aggressive for some high-latency regions; can we make it configurable per-region or per-deployment?
Priya: Timeout is now a runtime flag with a default of 150ms and override maps per-region in defaults.yaml. Added documentation entry explaining tradeoffs.
Anya: CI reported a flaky e2e timing test; looks like the probe race on shutdown can cause a goroutine leak. Please address.
Priya: Fixed probe goroutine lifecycle and added a cleanup hook in middleware. Re-ran CI; all green.
release_notes: Added an opt-in runtime schema probe for clients declaring X-Redwood-Schema: v3-beta. The probe enables safe v3 rollouts by detecting client capability and applying a runtime shim/fallback to v2 semantics when necessary. Metrics and canary rollout config included. No breaking changes; opt-in only.
notes_for_ops: To enable the feature for a canary, set runtime flag enable_schema_probe=true and canary_pct=5 in deploy/flags/runtime_flags.go or via runtime config service. Tune probe_timeout_ms for high-latency regions. Watch metrics openai_compat.schema_probe.* and dashboards/pkg/observability/dashboards/schema_probe.json for failures before increasing canary percentage.
post_merge_tasks: Create Linear ticket ENG-5032 to track 10% increments and monitor SLOs
Coordinate with Solutions to announce opt-in header to top 10 customers
Add console toggle in next release to control enable_schema_probe per-tenant
